title: Orestes: Vengeance and the Court
subtitle: A son must kill his mother — and the gods argue about justice

learningObjectives.text: What impossible duty is Orestes given?
How does the cycle of blood end?

narrativeBlocks.title: The son returns
narrativeBlocks.body: Orestes, smuggled out as a baby when his father was murdered, comes home grown — to a mother who is both the wronged wife of Agamemnon and the killer of his father. Every obligation pulls in opposite directions.

narrativeBlocks.title: Apollo's command
narrativeBlocks.body: The god of Delphi himself orders the revenge: kill Clytemnestra and Aegisthus. Matricide is the deepest pollution — and refusing vengeance is betrayal of the father. There is no clean act left in this family.

narrativeBlocks.title: The deed and the Furies
narrativeBlocks.body: Orestes kills both his mother and her lover — and immediately the Furies arrive: ancient earth-goddesses who pursue blood-kin killers. He is hounded across Greece, purified yet never free.

narrativeBlocks.title: Trial at Athens
narrativeBlocks.body: At the Areopagus, Athena convenes the first murder trial in myth: Apollo argues duty, the Furies argue blood. The jury of Athenians splits evenly — and Athena casts the deciding vote for acquittal.

narrativeBlocks.title: The court replaces the feud
narrativeBlocks.body: The play's real ending: blood-for-blood is replaced by legal process. The Furies are not defeated but honoured — renamed 'the Kindly Ones' and given a shrine. Vengeance doesn't end; it is institutionalised.
